# 1 Enoch Chapter 103 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Epistle of Enoch

---

**1** Now I swear to you, the righteous, by the majesty of His glory and by His power and greatness, and by the sovereignty of His majesty: I swear to you that I know a mystery and have read the heavenly tablets, and have seen the holy books, and have found written therein and inscribed regarding their souls.

**2** All goodness and joy and glory are prepared for them, and written down for the spirits of those who have died in righteousness; and manifold good shall be given to you in recompense for your labors, and your lot shall be far beyond the lot of the living.

**3** And the spirits of you who have died in righteousness shall live and rejoice, and their spirits shall not perish, nor their memorial from before the face of the Great One throughout all generations of the world; therefore fear their contempt no more.

**4** Woe to you, sinners, when you have died, if you die in the wealth of your sins, and those who are like you say regarding you: "Blessed are the sinners — they have seen all their days.

**5** And how they died in prosperity and wealth, and have not seen tribulation or murder in their life, and they have died in honor, and judgment was not executed on them during their life."

**6** Know that their souls will be made to descend into Sheol and they shall be wretched in their great tribulation.

**7** And into darkness and chains and a burning flame where there is grievous judgment shall their spirits enter, and the great judgment shall be for all the generations of the world. Woe to you, for you shall have no peace.

**8** Do not say regarding the righteous and good who are alive: "In our troubled days we toiled laboriously and experienced every trouble, and met with much evil and were consumed, and became few and our spirit grew small.

**9** And we have been destroyed and found no one to help us even with a word; we were tortured and destroyed, and had no hope of seeing life from day to day.

**10** We hoped to be the head and have become the tail; we toiled laboriously and had no satisfaction in our toil; and we have become the food of sinners and the unrighteous, and they have laid their yoke heavily upon us.

**11** Those who hated us had dominion over us and struck us, and to those who hated us we bowed our necks, but they pitied us not.

**12** We desired to get away from them that we might escape and be at rest, but found no place where we might flee and be safe from them.

**13** And we complained with weeping to the rulers in our tribulation and cried out against those who devoured us, but they did not attend to our cries and would not listen to our voice.

**14** And they helped those who robbed us and devoured us and made us few; they concealed their oppression and did not remove from us the yoke of those who devoured us and scattered us and murdered us, and they concealed their murder, and did not remember that they had lifted their hands against us."

**15** I swear to you, the righteous, that in heaven the angels remember you for good before the glory of the Great One; and your names are written before the glory of the Great One.

---

*LOGOS notes: Vv. 8–14 form an extended communal lament in the first person plural, one of the most detailed descriptions of social oppression in Second Temple literature. The complaint covers: judicial corruption (rulers who sided with oppressors, v. 14), loss of status (head become tail, v. 10), exploitative labor (v. 10), physical violence (v. 11), and the impossibility of escape (v. 12). V. 15's answer — the angels remember you — is the eschatological reversal of the earthly amnesia.*
